# Supermatter Stability
The Supermatter Crystal is equipped with an internal stability monitoring system.
If the crystal's structural stability decreases below an acceptable threshold, the monitoring system will automatically issue warnings through station communication systems.
The Supermatter can be damaged through multiple forms of interaction.
Physical contact with the crystal is extremely hazardous. Direct interaction causes structural disturbance and contributes to destabilization.
High-energy sources, including emitter-based laser systems, can transfer enough energy into the crystal to cause instability.
Environmental conditions also influence crystal stability.
Temperature, pressure, and atmospheric composition must be carefully monitored to maintain safe operation.
